LESSON: ROTATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CORE MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements and Geometry
Topic 2.3: Rotation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rotation, part of Measurements and Geometry in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 CORE MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How is rotation applied in real-life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. demonstrate rotation using an actual or improvised clock in purposive pairs or groups. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive technology or be assisted by peers/learner support

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. demonstrate rotation using an actual or improvised clock in purposive pairs or groups. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive technology or be assisted by peers/learner support

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rotation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and Problem Solving: as the learner draws objects and their images and through construction

establishes the centres and angles of rotation.

● Communication and Collaboration: as the learner discusses using an object and its image on a plane surface to

generate the properties of rotation.

34

Values:
● Responsibility: as the learner takes care of learning resources collected from the immediate environment to establish

their axis and order of rotational symmetry.

● Respect: as learners appreciate each other’s opinion as they discuss and draw the image under a rotation given the

object, center and angle of rotation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental education: as the learner responsibly collects regular solids from the immediate environment to

determine the axis and order of rotational symmetry.

Suggested Learning Resources

Geometrical instruments (padded compass/ dividers, rulers with enhanced grip, protractor with handle), metre rule

with handle, charts on multiplication tables, paper cut-outs of regular shapes made of heavy gauge papers, drawing/

manila/ graph papers, scissors with enhanced grip, multipurpose communication boards on regular objects of different

shapes and sizes, white boards, slant boards, book holders, head pointers, page turners, pen/pencil holders, adapted

scientific calculators/ projectors, adhesives, positioning devices such as special seats with straps, adapted digital

devices such as adapted computers with larger screens
